chunks: Abū Baṣīr asked him about a man who intends Makkah or al-Madīnah: is it disliked for him to go out with weapons? So he said:
"There is no harm in his going out with weapons from his town, but when he enters Makkah, he should not display them."

key_terms.أَبُو بَصِيرٍ: Abū Baṣīr, the narrator asking the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةَ: al-Madīnah, the city mentioned alongside Makkah in the question
key_terms.بَلَدِهِ: his town or hometown, from which he departs
key_terms.بِالسِّلَاحِ: with weapons; carrying arms during travel
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating permissibility
key_terms.لَمْ يُظْهِرْهُ: he should not display it; meaning the weapon should not be openly shown
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the sacred city to which the ruling specifically refers

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to carry weapons when traveling to Makkah or al-Madīnah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning carrying weapons while traveling to Makkah or al-Madīnah. It states that there is no harm in departing with weapons from one's hometown, but upon entering Makkah one should not display them, reflecting the sanctity and etiquette of the sacred precinct.
